guideTitle: 6 Best Lap Trays with Handles in 2026
metaTitle: Best Lap Trays with Handles in 2026
metaDescription: Six lap trays with handles compared by size, grip and rim depth, from a single large tray to multi packs and a hand-woven bamboo set for couch dining.
introParagraphs: A lap tray with handles is the tool that lets you eat dinner in a recliner, watch a game from the couch or take breakfast to a favorite chair without balancing a plate on your knees. The handles matter more here than on a table tray, because you lift the tray from a seated position, often with a hand that is also holding a remote or a glass. A good lap tray is wide enough for a plate and a cup, shallow enough to clear the knees and grippy enough that nothing slides when you shift.

The six trays here take different routes to the same goal. The Hodvya and Kazozobi both measure 17.7 by 12.5 inches, the Cedilis is about 16 by 11 inches, the Lyksgir is a deeper 15.7 by 11.2 inch tray in a pack of four, the Orpomea uses soft silicone nubs, and the PEMAR set is hand-woven bamboo in a size of about 17 by 13 inches. Some of these are sold as multi-packs, which suits a household where two or three people eat in front of the television together.

We evaluated each tray from the product page and maker specifications, without any hands-on claim. We focused on footprint, rim height, grip, handle shape and how easily the trays store when the meal is over.

products.name: Hodvya Large Non-Slip Lap Serving Tray with Handles
products.description:
The Hodvya is the lap tray that most households will be happy with. At 17.7 by 12.5 inches it holds a 10 inch dinner plate, utensils and a cup, which the maker states directly, and the size is large enough to feel generous without being too wide to rest across both knees. The handles are molded into the ends, giving you a firm grip on both sides.

The feature that sets it apart is the slip-resistant strips. They are placed on the bottom, the surface and the handles, so the tray grips your lap, your plate grips the tray and your hands grip the handles. The listing says the tray carries a maximum load of 25 pounds, which is far more than any meal, and describes it as lightweight yet sturdy. That combination matters for someone who cannot lift a heavy tray with a full dinner on it.

The tray is also stackable for storage, so it slides into a closet or beside the sofa. It is sold as a single piece, which suits one person; if you need two trays, you will need to buy two. Compared with the Kazozobi, which has the same footprint, the Hodvya puts more attention on grip. Compared with the Lyksgir, it is bigger and shallower. For one person eating on the couch, it is the first tray to consider. Rest it across both thighs rather than on one knee, and keep the heavier item toward the handle you hold with your stronger hand. When the meal is done, a quick wipe is usually enough, and the stackable shape means it fits behind a chair or in a closet.
products.bestFor: One person eating dinner in a chair.
pros: Holds a 10 inch plate and cup
Strips grip lap, plate and handles

products.name: Orpomea Large Non-Slip Lap Serving Tray, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Orpomea tray is built around its surface. Non-stick nubs cover the top, and the maker says they carry a glass or plate without sliding around. That is exactly what you want in a recliner, where the tray tilts every time you shift position and a smooth surface lets a cup drift toward the edge.

The set comes with two trays made of environmentally friendly plastic and silicone, and the listing calls them non-toxic and dishwasher safe, so cleanup after a meal is a matter of loading them with the dishes. The suggested uses include a snack or coffee, a bed tray for eating and a surface for a football match in a recliner. The trays have handles on both sides for lifting.

The nubs have a downside: a thin paper plate or a flat napkin does not sit evenly on them, and crumbs can collect between the dots, so a quick rinse is part of the routine. Against the Hodvya, the Orpomea is a pair rather than a single tray, and its grip is softer. Against the Kazozobi, which relies on textured plastic, the silicone nubs hold glassware better. Choose it for drinks and for two people sharing the sofa. A pair means each person has their own tray, so nobody has to pass a hot mug across a lap. Rinse the nubs under running water and let them air dry for the best result.
products.bestFor: Drinks and glassware on a couch.

products.name: Kazozobi X-Large Anti-Slip Lap Serving Trays, 3 Pack
products.description:
The Kazozobi gives you three large trays at the same 17.7 by 12.5 inch size as the Hodvya, with a rim height of 1.8 inches. The listing says each one holds a plate, a large drink, a plate of snacks and cutlery at once, which is a fair description of a full lap meal. Three trays suit a family that eats together in the living room.

The handles are the standout feature. The maker says each has two protective handles that are angled to match the natural grip angle, which makes them easier to grab and smoother to hold. That ergonomic detail is useful when you lift a loaded tray from your lap, because a wrongly angled handle makes you twist your wrist. The surface is non-slip plastic that helps hold plates in place.

The rim of 1.8 inches is deeper than the Cedilis, which helps contain spills, but it also means the tray sits higher on your lap. Compared with the Hodvya, the Kazozobi offers three trays instead of one, and compared with the Lyksgir it is wider but shallower. If you want matching trays for the whole family, it is the strongest value in the guide. Three trays also give you a spare when one is in the wash, so the household never has to wait on a clean tray. Pick the handle with your stronger hand when you lift, and keep the tray level as you stand.

products.name: Lyksgir Large Non-Slip Serving Trays with Rubber Handles, 4 Pack
products.description:
The Lyksgir is the deepest tray in this comparison, at 2.1 inches, and it comes in a pack of four. The extra depth keeps soup bowls, sauces and loose snacks from slipping over the edge, which matters when your lap is not a level surface. Each tray measures 15.7 by 11.2 inches, a little smaller than the Hodvya but still large enough for a plate and a cup.

The maker describes double anti-slip technology: grippy TPR rubber dots on the surface to hold plates and glasses, and wavy zigzag strips to add friction elsewhere. The handles are rubber, which gives a warm, non-slip hold even with damp hands. The trays are made from BPA-free, food-grade plastic and TPR rubber, and the listing says they are lightweight and heat-insulated.

Four trays suit a household that likes to eat together or a visitor heavy home. The trays are stackable, but the deeper rim means they take more shelf room than flatter trays. Compared with the Kazozobi, the Lyksgir is smaller and deeper. Compared with the Orpomea, it grips with rubber dots rather than silicone nubs. Choose it if you eat soups, sauces or anything that tends to slide. The heat-insulated plastic is also kinder to your thighs when a bowl of soup is hot. With four in the pack you can keep one set by the television and another near a reading chair, so the trays are always where you use them.

products.name: PEMAR Hand-Woven Natural Bamboo Trays with Handles, Set of 4
products.description:
The PEMAR set is the most decorative option here. Each tray is hand-woven from natural bamboo by artisans, so no two are exactly alike, and the four identical large trays measure about 17 by 13 inches. The listing says they stack neatly to save space, and that they work as dinner trays, bedside food trays or even vanity and spa trays.

The woven bamboo gives the tray a natural, warm look that suits a living room better than molded plastic. It is also lighter than most wooden trays. The tradeoff is that woven bamboo is a more open surface, so crumbs fall between the weave and liquids can soak in, and it needs more careful cleaning than plastic. It has handles, but they are woven into the frame and give a fingertip grip rather than a full hand wrap.

Compared with the Hodvya, the PEMAR is more attractive and less grippy. Compared with the Lyksgir, it has no deep rim. Choose it if you want a lap tray that looks good when it is left out and you mostly carry dry food.
products.bestFor: A tray that looks good left out.

products.name: Cedilis White Plastic Lap Serving Trays with Handles, 3 Pack
products.description:
The Cedilis is the lightest and flattest lap tray here. It measures 16 by 11 inches with a rim of 1.2 inches, and the listing describes it as lap-friendly and cafeteria-tray sized. Made of thick polypropylene that will not warp, splinter or shatter if dropped, it is a practical choice for rough daily use.

The surface has a non-slip texture that adds grip and hides scratches, and the raised rim helps keep plates, food and drinks from sliding off. Because the tray is shallow, it sits close to the lap, which is comfortable and keeps the load stable. The trays stack, so three of them take little space.

Compared with the Kazozobi, the Cedilis is slightly smaller and flatter. Compared with the PEMAR, it is less handsome and much easier to clean. Choose it if you want a no-fuss tray for TV dinners. Because it is light even when loaded, it is a good match for anyone who finds a heavy tray tiring to lift. The white color makes it easy to see when the surface needs a rinse. Three trays stack into a slim pile, so they hide easily beside a bookshelf.
cons: Smaller than the extra large trays

buyingCriteria.criterion: Size against your plate and lap
buyingCriteria.explanation: A lap tray must be wide enough for a plate and a cup, but not so wide that it hangs off your knees. The Hodvya and Kazozobi are 17.7 by 12.5 inches, the PEMAR is about 17 by 13 inches, the Cedilis is 16 by 11 inches and the Lyksgir is 15.7 by 11.2 inches. Measure the width of your lap while seated and compare. A tray that overhangs tips when you lean.

Handles are the feature that separates a lap tray from a plate. The Kazozobi lists an ergonomic handle angle, the Lyksgir has rubber handles and the Hodvya has slip-resistant strips on the handles. A handle that is too thin or too slick makes you squeeze, and that is when drinks spill. Check whether the handle lets all your fingers fit comfortably.

A deeper rim contains spills but raises the tray. The Lyksgir is 2.1 inches deep, the Kazozobi is 1.8 inches and the Cedilis is 1.2 inches. For soup and sauces, choose the deeper trays, and for dry snacks a shallow rim is more comfortable. A very deep tray can also make it harder to reach the food.

Lap trays tilt constantly, so surface grip is vital. The Orpomea has silicone nubs, the Lyksgir has TPR rubber dots, the Hodvya has strips, and the PEMAR has a plain woven surface. Rubber and silicone hold glassware best. Smooth bamboo is the weakest at gripping.

Plastic and silicone are easiest to clean, and the Orpomea is listed as dishwasher safe. Bamboo, as in the PEMAR, needs hand washing and drying. Look for BPA-free, food-grade materials on any tray that touches food directly. A tray that goes in the dishwasher saves effort after a messy meal, while a tray that must be hand washed will be used less often. Think honestly about which routine you will keep.

Packs of 2, 3 or 4 suit households that eat together. A single Hodvya suits one person. Stackable trays such as the Hodvya, Cedilis and PEMAR save space, while deeper trays like the Lyksgir take more room. Pick a spot for storage before you buy, such as beside the sofa or in a closet, so the tray is within reach when dinner is ready.

faq.q: How do I choose a lap tray size?
faq.a: Measure the width of your lap while seated and add a bit for the handles. The Hodvya and Kazozobi at 17.7 inches wide suit most adults. A smaller tray such as the Lyksgir fits a narrower lap.
A deeper rim contains spills but raises the tray. The Lyksgir at 2.1 inches suits soup. The Cedilis at 1.2 inches suits dry snacks.

faq.q: Can I put lap trays in the dishwasher?
faq.a: The Orpomea lists itself as dishwasher safe. Plastic trays are easy to hand wash, and bamboo like the PEMAR must be washed by hand and dried. Always check the listing before using a dishwasher, since high heat can warp thin plastic.

faq.q: Do lap trays work on a bed?
faq.a: Yes, several are sold for bed use. A lap tray rests on your legs, so choose one with a flat base. Folding leg bed tables are a different product.

faq.q: How much weight can a lap tray hold?
faq.a: The Hodvya lists a maximum load of 25 pounds. Most meals weigh far less. Check each listing for load limits if you plan to place heavy items.

faq.q: Which tray is best for glasses?
faq.a: The Orpomea with silicone nubs and the Lyksgir with TPR dots hold glassware well. A smooth surface lets a glass slide when you tilt. Even with a grippy tray, fill cups only about three quarters full and carry slowly.

faq.q: How should I store lap trays?
faq.a: Stack them, as the Hodvya, Cedilis and PEMAR allow, and keep them near the sofa. Deeper trays like the Lyksgir need more room. Do not stack heavy objects on top of plastic trays, because the rim can crack.
